acceptance: validate gives an agents: notice when CLAUDE.md exists, root AGENTS.md has project text outside its managed block, and CLAUDE.md does not import @AGENTS.md, saying Claude Code never reads that text and naming the line to add; no notice when the import is present or AGENTS.md is only the block

The load-order section of .specyrd/AGENTS.md states in one sentence that it is a default a project may replace, and that roadmap-context.md first is the one step to keep. validate gives a notice when the project's own AGENTS.md text defines a load order (a numbered list under a heading containing 'load order'), naming the entries in specy-road's load order that it omits (roadmap-context.md first)

When CLAUDE.md imports both @AGENTS.md and @.specyrd/AGENTS.md and the root block is the full one, the notice says the floor bullets are read twice, gives the duplicated bytes, and names agents_block: minimal (M13.3) as the fix; it never suggests dropping the .specyrd import
Each notice is pinned by a fixture test and none rewrites project files. Out of scope: merging or reordering project load orders, and the paragraph-level duplicate report (M13.11)

upgrade runs validate, so the missing-import notice appears in upgrade's output too; a test runs upgrade on a fixture with project text outside the block and no @AGENTS.md import in CLAUDE.md and asserts the notice and the exact line to add, and a fixture where AGENTS.md is only the block prints none

The AGENTS.md migration notice and .specyrd/AGENTS.md's addenda paragraph say that repo-specific specy-road rules, including such text found outside the markers, belong in .specyrd/AGENTS.team.md; agents_md_block.py (392 lines) changes wording only, with no net lines; a test pins the sentence
nodes.title: Notices for how the agent files fit together: missing CLAUDE.md import, two load orders, floor read twice

acceptance: upgrade prints the M13.8 catalogue entries newer than the version stamped in the managed block it replaced (or the repo's pin when there is no block), one line each; none when the stamp is current; a test with an older stamp pins the list

When the repo's pin (manifest pin or a requirements file) is below the minimum upgrade just wrote into the managed block, upgrade says so plainly, naming the pin's file and both versions. A release-candidate trial is recorded as a 'pin_trial' key in .specyrd/manifest.json naming the trialled version (set by the project, documented in the upgrade guide; no CLI flag); while the running version equals pin_trial, validate prints the pin mismatch once as a trial note instead of a warning, and the key is ignored (warning returns) once the running version changes; a test covers the warning, the trial note and its expiry

upgrade's closing hint names the kinds of new untracked files it actually created (schemas, model profiles, skills, .specyrd/ files) instead of always saying 'schema and skill files'; a test where only schemas are new pins it

upgrade --report-duplicates lists paragraphs of project text outside the managed block that closely restate a paragraph of .specyrd/AGENTS.md (normalised word overlap above a stated threshold), naming file:line and the matching rules heading; report only. Out of scope: rewriting or deleting project text, and the heading-level notice M13.3 owns
nodes.title: upgrade says what changed for this repo: behaviour changes, a pin below the new minimum, the new files and duplicated paragraphs
